campaign_name: See It First - proof before payment

cadence.set_by: Six drops across eight days (2026-09-06 to 2026-09-13), no two on the same day, rotating across morning, midday, and evening dayparts. interval_minutes is the mean gap and is documentation only; each drop's scheduled_time is authoritative.

cadence_collision_note: Every scheduled_time carries a :07 seconds offset on purpose. scripts/queue-campaign-drops.py groups Postiz sibling records by exact publishDate string when converting drafts to a live schedule, so a drop sharing a timestamp to the second with another campaign's drop would pull that campaign's records into this one's conversion. Three other campaigns were built in parallel on 2026-09-05; the seconds offset makes a collision impossible rather than unlikely.

publish_arming.note: Queue creates DRAFTS unarmed. Conversion to a live schedule requires FAMTASTIC_MARKETING_PUBLISH=true on the operator host. Nothing in this campaign has been queued; the owner holds the publish gate.

media_resolution.note: Every primary_media here is a committed PNG, not a gitignored video, so no drop should ever block on missing media. A drop whose media is missing is reported BLOCKED with the expected path rather than posted image-less.

channel_targeting_note: Facebook and Instagram only. YouTube's OAuth token is expired and TikTok is not approved for public posting; both need the owner. Requesting them here would manufacture BLOCKED rows for channels that cannot publish today.

drops.label: Drop 1 - 10:20 AM ET: the objection, answered by the order of operations
drops.headline: See it first. Then decide.

copy.facebook_instagram:
"I have been burned before."

That is the most honest reason a business owner gives for not building a website, and it is a fair one. You paid, you waited, and what came back was not what you pictured.

So we changed the order.

FAMtastic builds three design directions from your real business information. A person reviews them before you ever see them. Then you open them in a private, view-only link - no account, no login - and look at the actual work.

You decide from something on your screen, not from a description in an email.

Nobody should be asked for money against a promise.

How proof-first works:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/proof-first-website-see-before-you-pay/

drops.label: Drop 2 - 12:50 PM ET: published scope, including the boundaries
drops.theme: A promise is not a proof
drops.headline: A promise is not a proof.

copy.facebook_instagram:
A promise is a sentence. A proof is your site, on your screen.

The difference shows up in the part nobody enjoys reading: what is actually included, and what is not.

Web Basics is one focused landing-page website, one year of managed hosting, and first-year domain registration - or connecting a domain you already own. That is the whole bundle. Business email is a separate product. Maintenance is an add-on, not a quiet inclusion.

$199 covers the first year. After that, hosting renews at $9.99 a month and the domain renews separately.

We would rather you read the boundaries now than find them later.

What the $199 website includes, and what it does not:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/199-website-inclusions-and-boundaries/

drops.label: Drop 3 - 8:20 AM ET: the promise we refuse to make
drops.headline: Do you guarantee Google rankings? No.

copy.facebook_instagram:
Do you guarantee Google rankings?

No.

Nobody can hand you a ranking, and anyone who promises one is promising something they do not control. We would rather lose the sale than make that promise.

Here is what we will do instead. Build the page so a search engine can actually read it. Tell you plainly what it can and cannot affect. And show you the work before you pay for it.

An honest no is worth more than a confident maybe. If you have been burned before, it was usually by the maybe.

The full answer:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/do-you-guarantee-google-rankings/

drops.label: Drop 4 - 5:50 PM ET: the five published steps
drops.theme: Trust is a sequence you can see
drops.headline: What happens, in order

copy.facebook_instagram:
What makes a business website feel trustworthy is boring on purpose. An address you own. A price you can read without asking for it. And a process you can see the shape of before you commit to it.

Here is ours, in order:

Intake - your real business details, not a template's placeholder text.
Proof - three directions, reviewed by a person before you see them.
Revision - you say what to change.
Approval - you sign off.
Launch - it goes live.

Five steps, published rather than improvised. You can hold us to a list you were shown first.

What makes a business website feel trustworthy:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/what-makes-business-website-trustworthy/

drops.label: Drop 5 - 11:20 AM ET: the silence after you pay
drops.headline: Nothing happens in the dark.

copy.facebook_instagram:
The worst part of hiring anybody is the silence after you pay.

So there is no silence.

You fill in an intake about your real business. We build three directions from it. A person reviews them before you see them. You open them in a private, view-only link, say what you want changed, and approve the one you want. Then it launches.

Every one of those steps ends with you doing something, which is why you are never left guessing where your project is.

What happens after you buy:
https://famtasticdesigns.com/blog/after-buying-199-website/
